The native engine guide

Source: vignettes/articles/native-guide.qmd

The native engine fits models from lavaan-style syntax by maximum likelihood, with a covariance structure and, when you write intercepts, observed means. This guide covers the whole workflow in one place: syntax, fitting, inference, constraints, model comparison, diagnostics and the route to the mediation objects. For a first look, read the five-minute quickstart.

Entry points fit_sem(syntax, data); fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native") for one mediator
Class returned SEMFit, then MediationData, SerialMediationData or ParallelMediationData from extract_mediation()
Syntax reference ?"medfit-syntax"
Not covered latent means, latent products, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators; see the limits 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
d <- mediation_demo

1. Syntax

Statement Meaning
y ~ x1 + x2 regression of y on x1 and x2
f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 latent variable f measured by indicators
y1 ~~ y2 covariance; y1 ~~ y1 is a variance
y ~ a*x label a path; equal labels are one parameter
y ~ 0.5*x fix a path
start(0.3)*, lower(0)*, upper(1)* starting value, lower and upper bound
ab := a*b defined parameter with a delta-method standard error
a == b, cp == a*b, a*b > 0.1 equality or inequality constraint on labels, linear or not
y1, y2 ~ x comma shorthand (a medfit extension; lavaan reads it differently)

Exogenous observed variables are fixed at their sample moments by default, as lavaan does with fixed.x = TRUE (fewer parameters, the same structural estimates, a conditional log likelihood); fixed_x = FALSE in fit_sem() gives them free variances and covariances instead. Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition are arithmetic expressions in the labels (+ - * / ^, parentheses, exp, log, sqrt, abs, min, max, pnorm, qnorm, and a few more).

2. Fit and read 

syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d)
summary(fit)

The chi-square is \(n\) times the minimized discrepancy and has df degrees of freedom. A saturated model (here df = 0) fits perfectly by construction, so the test only means something when there are restrictions.

3. Standard errors and weights

The default information matrix is observed; information = "expected" gives lavaan’s default. se_type = "sandwich" gives the HC0 robust covariance, and weights takes case weights.

w <- seq_len(nrow(d)) %% 3 + 1
robust <- fit_sem(syntax, d, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
rbind(model_based = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))[1:3], weighted_robust = sqrt(diag(vcov(robust)))[1:3])
                         a mediator1~covariate1          b
model_based     0.09858458           0.04833820 0.05306479
weighted_robust 0.10207525           0.04774111 0.06498487

4. Constraints

A constraint is a line of syntax. The engine classifies it and uses the cheapest exact route:

Constraint Example How it is solved
linear equality or bound a == b, a + b == 1, a < 0.3 constant Jacobian rows; every accepted solution passes a gate on all rows
nonlinear equality cp == a*b Jacobian recomputed at every point; every start tried, the best accepted one kept; a Newton polish after acceptance
nonlinear inequality a*b > 0.1, ab > 0 with ab := a*b same, as rows \(c(\theta) \le 0\); a warning when the starts disagree
one independent nonzero product a*b == 0.1 both sign domains searched; an unresolved required branch stops the fit; coverage is not global optimality
product set to zero a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0 exact: one linear fit per factor, smallest discrepancy kept
sum of products a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0 best-effort: the best of the starts; a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, so raise n_starts 
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), d)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
     a      b     cp
0.5423 0.5497 0.2981 
tied@diagnostics$active_constraints
[1] "cp == a * b"

Labels used in a constraint must be defined in the model, and a constraint with no free parameter is an error. CONSTRAINT(a == b) is the same as the bare a == b.

5. Compare models and test the indirect effect

anova() is the likelihood-ratio test for nested SEMFits; it refits nothing. Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, a necessary condition, so two models that pass but are not nested in substance are your responsibility. mbco_sem() tests an indirect effect that is a product of paths:

anova(tied, fit)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

     Df Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit   0 0.000
tied  1 0.938    0.93802       1     0.3328
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 33.353, df = 1, p-value = 7.685e-09

For a chain a, d, b, give the paths: mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b")) is the minimum of the single-path tests against a chi-square with one degree of freedom. The null is a union of hypotheses, so the test is conservative when more than one path is zero (its size is at most 0.055 at the 5% level in the package’s simulation gate).

6. Diagnostics

Read these before trusting a fit; all are in summary(fit) and fit@diagnostics:

Field What it says If it is wrong
Converged the optimizer returned and the acceptance gate passed the fit is not returned; the error names the failure
Optimizer status, stationarity the solver’s code and the Newton decrement at the solution a large decrement means a stall; try n_starts
Active bounds / Active constraints which bounds or constraints bind a binding bound means the estimate is on the edge
Improper solution a negative variance or non-positive definite covariance respecify, or bound the variance
Multiplier sign check active inequality multipliers have the right sign a wrong sign means an active bound was not optimal 
b <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome\n"), d)
b@diagnostics$active_bounds
[1] "outcome~~outcome"

For the nonzero-product supported shapes, local-search limits and coverage record, see the constraints page.

When a model with a nonlinear constraint warns that the starts reached different optima, the constraint has more than one solution (a*b > 0.1 holds for two positive or two negative paths). The kept fit is the best, but say so in a report.

The outcome ledger

Every native fit keeps a versioned record of how it was reached, fit@diagnostics$ledger: one node per fit, zero-product branch and mbco_sem() null, each with its optimizer state, likelihood, covariance status and notices. A node is resolved (the optimizer accepted it) or unresolved, and unresolved means unknown: only a feasibility of certified_empty is a proof that a branch has no solution, and only a literal contradiction such as a == 0 with a == 1 earns it. Errors that stop a fit carry the same ledger as $ledger, and mbco_sem() and compare_lr() return it with an unresolved result. Read it with str(fit@diagnostics$ledger, max.level = 2); the cases and what to do are in Troubleshooting, and the construction is in Computation and algorithms.

7. From a fit to mediation objects 

x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
[1] "medfit::MediationData"

fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native", treatment =, mediator =) does both steps for one mediator. For several mediators, fit with fit_sem() and call extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c("m1", "m2"), outcome = ): a chain gives a SerialMediationData, mediators side by side a ParallelMediationData. A latent mediator works through the same call.

Limits

  • Observed means only. Intercepts (y ~ 1, y ~ 1 + x) are estimated for observed variables; a free latent mean or intercept stops with “latent means are planned for a later release”.
  • One group; listwise deletion is the missing-data default. The separate bounded FIML opt-in retains partially observed rows only for its random-X model: X, M and Y, with up to two covariates.
  • ML only, plus the HC0 sandwich; no robust chi-square, no fit indices beyond the chi-square, AIC and BIC.
  • Products (x:m, which give the four-way decomposition) work for two observed variables inside a supported class; the table of limits and messages is on the native model page. The model test is NA when a product factor is a regression target.
  • AIC and BIC of a fit with a product are not comparable with those of a fit without one (the product column enters the likelihood), so AIC(fit_a, fit_b) and BIC() refuse such a pair; see the native model page.
  • For latent means, groups, categorical outcomes or fit indices use lavaan; the extraction route accepts a lavaan fit as well. See lavaan and the native engine.

Bounded FIML (0.16.0)

Bounded FIML was introduced in 0.16.0 and is unavailable in released 0.15.0. Ordinary calls still delete incomplete model rows listwise. The explicit opt-in below fits numeric continuous observed variables: X to M to Y (three variables) with a free or exactly zero direct path, independent Gaussian disturbances and free intercepts. After 0.16.0 the development version also fits the same model with one covariate or two covariates (see covariates), two parallel mediators (see parallel mediators) and the two-mediator serial forms, saturated or pure chain, with up to two covariates (see serial mediators). It assumes ignorable missingness under that joint model; FIML does not impute the missing values.

Generate continuous Gaussian X, M and Y with independent disturbances for this example; the bundled demo’s binary treatment does not match this joint model. The fixed missing-value pattern is for illustration, not evidence that missingness in an applied study is ignorable. with_seed() preserves the caller’s random-number state.

fiml_data <- withr::with_seed(271L, {
  n <- 400L
  treatment <- .8 + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 1.1)
  mediator1 <- -.4 + .5 * treatment + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .8)
  outcome <- .7 + .6 * mediator1 + .25 * treatment + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .9)
  data.frame(treatment = treatment, mediator1 = mediator1, outcome = outcome)
})
fiml_data$mediator1[seq(1, nrow(fiml_data), by = 7)] <- NA_real_
fiml_syntax <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment
outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
fiml_fit <- medfit::fit_sem(
  fiml_syntax, fiml_data, missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE,
  meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed", se_type = "model"
)
c(retained_rows = nobs(fiml_fit), logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fiml_fit)))
retained_rows        logLik
      400.000     -1544.246 
fiml_effects <- extract_mediation(fiml_fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
nie(fiml_effects)
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2795
nde(fiml_effects)
Natural Direct Effect (NDE): 0.2474
te(fiml_effects)
Total Effect (TE): 0.5269
tidy(fiml_effects, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term  estimate std_error
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.279    0.0365
2 nde      0.247    0.0508
3 te       0.527    0.0457

The wrapper route returns the extracted mediation object directly:

fiml_wrapped <- medfit::fit_mediation(
  model = fiml_syntax, data = fiml_data,
  treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1", engine = "native",
  se_type = "model", engine_args = list(
    missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed"
  )
)
tidy(fiml_wrapped, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term  estimate std_error
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.279    0.0365
2 nde      0.247    0.0508
3 te       0.527    0.0457

There is no new top-level missing argument on fit_mediation(); med() remains a formula-building fitter. The missing-method strings must match exactly. A failed FIML fit never falls back to listwise deletion or another engine, even on complete data.

Setting Bounded FIML requirement
fixed_x Explicit FALSE; omission, TRUE and named subsets refuse
meanstructure TRUE; NULL and FALSE refuse
information, se_type "observed", "model"
Weights No non-NULL vector, including unit weights or the deprecated alias
n_starts, control NULL or 3; empty control; no syntax-supplied starts
Topology X, M, Y, with at most two covariates, or X, M1, M2, Y (two parallel mediators, with at most two covariates, or the saturated serial graph or the pure chain, with up to two covariates); free or exactly zero direct path; no :=, constraints, ties, bounds, other extra predictors, latent variables, factors or products

The start/control restrictions preserve the initial validated protocol, rather than expressing mathematical limits of FIML. Three starts run for each solver; six attempt groups normally involve nine actual calls with nlminb refinements. Failures and completed calls are retained separately. Numerical acceptance requires both solvers, stationarity, agreeing likelihoods, local rank and valid observed information; it does not certify a global optimum or inference coverage.

Rows with any observed model variable are retained, including singleton patterns; only all-empty model rows are dropped. Extra columns do not select rows. No complete-case initialization is used: data with no complete rows can fit when local identification checks pass. nobs() counts retained rows, not observed cells. Original positional row IDs and pattern/count evidence are retained.

coef(), full vcov(), nobs(), raw logLik(), AIC/BIC, print/summary, parameter tidy and normal confidence intervals work on the SEMFit. Its glance() reports likelihood/IC fields, with model-test fields unavailable and an explicit reason. The discrepancy f and model-test df are NA; the separate free-parameter count is eight or nine (three variables; 13 or 14 and 19 or 20 with one and two covariates; 12 or 13 and 13 or 14 for parallel mediators with independent residuals and with a free residual covariance; without or with the direct path). There is no saturated missing-data fit. See Methods and Formulas for the likelihood.

Covariates

Development version only; not in 0.16.0. The opt-in also fits one covariate Z, or two covariates Z1 and Z2, written as M ~ X + Z and Y ~ M + X + Z (two covariates: M ~ X + Z1 + Z2, Y ~ M + X + Z1 + Z2). The exogenous variables have a free joint covariance with independent disturbances, and any variable may be incomplete. The rules:

  • Write every exogenous covariance pair (either order) or none. A partial set would fix the unwritten pairs at zero, so it is refused rather than completed.
  • Every exogenous variable needs a written path to Y, and every covariate path to M is free. Omitting a Y path is refused.
  • With no Y path fixed at zero, extract_mediation() may name any exogenous variable as the treatment. With exactly one Y path fixed at zero (0*X), that variable is the treatment.
  • Three or more covariates, a covariate on one equation only, residual covariances, constraints, ties, products and serial mediators remain refused. Covariates combined with two parallel mediators are covered in the next section.

These fits are implemented and numerically verified against lavaan and an independent likelihood. They are not calibrated for coverage and not statistically admitted, so the normal (delta-method) intervals carry the same caveat as the three-variable fit. bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = ) is withheld for every FIML fit, and a covariate fit is additionally refused by its own error (medfit_error_fiml_covariate_source_fit).

Parallel mediators

Development version only; not in 0.16.0. The opt-in also fits two parallel mediators, written M1 ~ X, M2 ~ X and Y ~ M1 + M2 (the direct path Y ~ X is free, fixed at exactly zero, or omitted). Any variable may be incomplete. The rules:

  • Independent residuals need the statement M1 ~~ 0*M2 (either order). Omitting the statement is refused: lavaan’s default would free that covariance, so silence is ambiguous.
  • A free, label-less M1 ~~ M2 fits the mediator residual covariance. A labeled, fixed nonzero, bounded, tied or otherwise constrained covariance is refused.
  • The free-parameter count is 12 or 13 with independent residuals and 13 or 14 with the free covariance, without or with a free direct path.
  • extract_mediation(fit, treatment = , mediator = c("M1", "M2")) names both mediators and returns a FIMLParallelMediationData object. Its covariance is the fitted full covariance of a1, a2, b1, b2 and c_prime, so the standard error of the sum of the indirect effects keeps the cross-path terms (unlike separate regressions). A refused extraction has class medfit_error_fiml_extract_unsupported.
  • With one covariate Z (or two, Z1 and Z2), write M1 ~ X + Z, M2 ~ X + Z and Y ~ M1 + M2 + X + Z, plus the mediator residual statement above. The covariate rules are those of the covariates section: every exogenous variable has a free path to both mediators and a written path to Y (omitting the direct path is therefore refused), the exogenous covariance pairs are all written or none, one Y path may be fixed at zero (that variable is then the treatment), and extract_mediation() may name any exogenous variable as the treatment otherwise. The free-parameter count is 18 to 20 with one covariate and 25 to 27 with two (without or with the direct path and the free residual covariance).
  • Three or more mediators, three or more covariates and a covariate on only some of the equations remain refused (serial mediators have their own section).

Like the covariate fits, these are implemented and numerically verified but not calibrated for coverage or statistically admitted. Delta-method Wald intervals for paths and effects are available. bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = ) is withheld by medfit_error_fiml_inference_unavailable; behind that guard a parallel fit has no source-fit route either (medfit_error_fiml_parallel_source_fit; with covariates medfit_error_fiml_covariate_source_fit).

Serial mediators

Development version only; not in 0.16.0. The opt-in also fits two serial mediators in two forms, each with no, one or two covariates: the saturated forward graph M1 ~ X, M2 ~ M1 + X and Y ~ M1 + M2 + X, and the pure chain M1 ~ X, M2 ~ M1 and Y ~ M2 (in both the direct path Y ~ X is free, fixed at exactly zero, or omitted). The rules:

  • The independence of all three disturbance pairs must be written: M1 ~~ 0*M2, M1 ~~ 0*Y and M2 ~~ 0*Y (either order within a pair). Omitting a statement is refused, and a free, labeled or nonzero one is refused as correlated disturbances. lavaan 0.7-3 frees none of these covariances for such models, so the written statement mirrors the parallel form rather than overriding a default.
  • Both shortcut paths, X -> M2 and M1 -> Y, are written and free (the saturated graph) or both are absent (the pure chain); one shortcut only, and a fixed or labeled shortcut, are refused.
  • The saturated model has 14 free parameters (13 with the direct path fixed at zero). With the direct path free it equals the unrestricted multivariate normal in parameters (the fit is a reparameterization of it), so it cannot misfit, and a pair of variables that is never observed together leaves that covariance undetermined: the fit fails closed with a medfit_sem_fiml_error at the numerical stage. A parallel fit that is accepted on the same data can therefore be refused here.
  • The pure chain has 12 free parameters (11 with the direct path fixed at zero) against 14 moments, so it has 2 (3) degrees of freedom: it is a restriction (X -> M2 and M1 -> Y are zero) that the data can reject, and its log-likelihood is at most the saturated one. Its structural zeros pin some covariances, so it can fit where the saturated graph fails closed.
  • extract_mediation(fit, treatment = , mediator = c("M1", "M2")) names both mediators in the fitted order (the reversed order is refused) and returns a FIMLSerialMediationData object. Its covariance is the fitted full covariance of a, a2, d1, b1, b and c_prime (the chain: a, d1, b and c_prime; no a2 or b1 exist). nie() is the chain effect a * d1 * b; for the saturated graph nie(type = "total") is a * d1 * b + a2 * b + a * b1, for the chain it is the same effect, and te() adds c_prime. Every estimated path is listed by paths(), tidy(), coef(type = "paths") and summary(); c_prime is listed with value 0 and standard error 0 when it is fixed. A refused extraction has class medfit_error_fiml_extract_unsupported.
  • At an exact origin the standard error of an indirect effect is withheld only where its delta gradient is zero: the chain effect when at least two of a, d1, b are zero, the saturated total indirect effect when a, a2, b and b1 are all zero. In the pure chain both indirect rows are the same effect and are withheld together, when at least two of a, d1, b are zero. Fits never produce exact zeros; this concerns constructed objects.
  • With one covariate Z, it predicts M1, M2 and Y in both forms (M1 ~ X + Z, M2 ~ M1 + X + Z or M2 ~ M1 + Z, Y ~ ... + X + Z), X and Z have a free covariance, and every exogenous variable needs a written Y path (free; at most one fixed at exactly zero, which makes that variable the treatment). The saturated model then has 20 free parameters (19 with the direct path fixed) and the chain 18 (17). The covariate’s coefficients are never paths: the extracted aliases are the treatment’s. In the saturated graph with a free direct path a covariate may be named the treatment (it takes a = Z -> M1, a2 = Z -> M2, c_prime = Z -> Y); in the pure chain the treatment is structural, the one exogenous variable with no path to M2, and naming a covariate is refused.
  • With two covariates Z1 and Z2 both predict every equation, the three exogenous covariances (X ~~ Z1, X ~~ Z2, Z1 ~~ Z2) are all written or none (a partial set is refused with a reason that names it), and the saturated model has 27 free parameters (26) and the chain 25 (24). Either covariate may be the saturated treatment when the direct path is free; with a fixed-zero direct path only the variable carrying the fixed zero is valid and naming another one is refused with a message saying so. In the chain, leaving a variable out of the equation of M2 makes it the treatment, and exactly one variable may be left out.
  • Serial models with three or more covariates remain refused, as do three or more mediators.

Like the other bounded fits, this one is implemented and numerically verified but not calibrated for coverage or statistically admitted. Delta-method Wald intervals for paths and effects are available; pm(), quick(), glance() and bootstrap intervals are refused for the extracted object, and bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = ) is withheld by medfit_error_fiml_inference_unavailable (behind that guard a serial fit is refused with medfit_error_fiml_serial_source_fit).

Extraction preserves validated FIML context through copying and serialization. Original SEMFit labels/full covariance stay unchanged; extracted a/b/c_prime and m_/y_ aliases follow topology, with original coordinates retained in context. Supported extracted operations are paths(), nie(), nde(), te(), coef() (paths/effects/all), full vcov(), print/summary, tidy and normal path/effect confidence intervals. At a = b = 0 the NIE point value is retained but its inferential fields are unavailable. A fixed direct path of zero instead has known zero covariance; other valid effect inference remains available.

Implemented but currently withheld (the call is refused pending admission; covariate and parallel fits have no source-fit route): bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = fiml_fit, effect = "nie", method = "nonparametric") uses the original accepted source fit for a retained-row FIML percentile interval. Explicit method = "parametric" instead gives a joint Gaussian parameter-draw percentile interval with no refits. Both use the original point estimate and type-7 quantiles; any required failed or interrupted replicate withholds all intervals and distribution SD while preserving the full requested ledger. Statistical admission and coverage calibration remain deferred. These methods were added after 0.16.0; see bootstrap_mediation() and Methods and Formulas for assumptions, conditional retention target and covariance handling.

Extracted-object glance(), quick(), pm(), extracted-object boot intervals, profiles, MBCO, fit tests, fit indices and prediction/residual APIs are deferred and refuse FIML objects. Package object-aware guards act before package-controlled refits, RNG or worker launch; opaque user callbacks are outside this guarantee. AIC/BIC comparisons dispatched with SEMFit first require compatible FIML contexts and refuse external/mixed objects before external likelihood calls. Calls dispatched first through another class are outside medfit’s guard.
